title: Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (Amendment) Bill
what_it_is: Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (Amendment) Bill

sections.label: IRAS grant disbursement role
sections.summary: The proposed amendments to the IRAS Act aim to formalise IRAS' role as a grant disbursement agency alongside its role as tax administrator.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Given the continued importance of this function, both in steady state and in crisis, the proposed amendments to the IRAS Act aim to formalise IRAS' role as a grant disbursement agency, alongside its role as tax administrator.

sections.label: IRAS enforcement powers for grants
sections.summary: The amendments would give IRAS enforcement powers to investigate serious grant offences, including accessing premises, inspections, seizing documents and making arrests.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: To enable IRAS to be more effective in this role, we propose to amend the IRAS Act to provide IRAS with enforcement powers to investigate serious grant offences, including the power to access premises, conduct inspections, seize documents and make arrests.

sections.label: Recovering overpaid grants and interest
sections.summary: The third amendment gives IRAS powers to recover overpaid grants as a debt due to the Government and impose interest on outstanding amounts.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The third key amendment provides IRAS with the powers to recover overpaid grants as a debt due to the Government, and to impose interest on outstanding amounts beyond the prescribed payment period.

sections.label: Powers to disburse grants, mitigate fraud
sections.summary: These powers allow IRAS to more effectively disburse grant schemes and mitigate the risk of fraud and abuse.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Together, these powers allow IRAS to more effectively disburse the various grant schemes and mitigate the risk of fraud and abuse.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The proposed legislative amendments are necessary to empower IRAS to do so effectively.

sections.label: Penalty for grant offences
sections.summary: The Bill allows IRAS to impose a penalty equivalent to or three times the amount that would have been given under the grant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Bill also allows IRAS to impose a penalty equivalent to or three times of the amount that would have been given under the grant.

sections.label: Imprisonment terms for false information
sections.summary: The imprisonment term is three years for offences under section 17F(3) and section 17F(5), and a Minister is asked to clarify their calibration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The imprisonment term is three years for offences under section 17F(3) for negligently providing false information and section 17F(5) for providing false information willfully with intent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can Minister clarify how the imprisonment term for section 17F(3) and section 17F(5) should be calibrated since the maximum imprisonment term is the same, but the culpability for offending under section 17F(5) is higher?

sections.label: IRAS tax collection costs
sections.summary: Tax collection cost fell to around 0.63 cents per dollar in FY2022 from 0.82 cents two years ago, as collections rose about 38% to $68.2 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In recent years, this has come off quite significantly, to around 0.63 cents per for every dollar collected in FY2022, from 0.82 cents just two years ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This perhaps is also reflective of the significant increases in IRAS' tax collections over the last two years, a jump of around 38% to $68.2 billion in FY2022, with FY2023 set to be another record year of tax collections, as we could soon find out in the upcoming Budget debate.

sections.label: Recovery of wrongly paid funds
sections.summary: The Government recovered over 99% of the S$370 million wrongly paid to companies, mostly through offsets against later Jobs Support Scheme payouts and cash returns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Subsequently, it was reported that the Government has recovered over 99% of the S$370 million wrongly paid to companies, with the bulk of it recovered through offsets against firms' subsequent Jobs Support Scheme payouts, where applicable, as well as returns in cash by large enterprises.

sections.label: COVID-19 grant abuse reports
sections.summary: From March 2020 to December 2021, Police received 57 reports of abuse or fraudulent application of COVID-19 Government grants and payouts, involving about S$1.7 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In response to a Parliamentary Question on cases involving the abuse, misuse or fraudulent application of COVID-19 Government grants and payouts, it was shared by the Minister for Home Affairs that from March 2020 to December 2021, the Police received 57 reports involving the abuse or fraudulent application of COVID-19 Government grants and payouts, involving approximately S$1.7 million.

sections.label: Recovered grants and SkillsFuture fraud
sections.summary: Questions were asked on amounts recovered from false claims and SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit disbursement, noting a syndicate defrauded SkillsFuture of about $40 million and amended legislation passed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: From these schemes, what is the total amount of money, credit, rebate or other grants recovered so far from falsely or wrongly given claims?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Thirdly, for Skillfuture Enterprise Credit, how do we ensure the grants that are provided are effectively disbursed?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We know of the syndicate that defrauded Skillsfuture of about $40 million and last year, in January, Parliament passed the amended SkillsFuture Singapore Agency and Skills Development Levy Act so prevent the abuse of Skillsfuture funding.

sections.label: Proposed penalty for offences
sections.summary: The proposed penalty can be equal to three times the amount received or imprisonment not exceeding three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Lastly, the penalty proposed can be equal to three times the amount received or an imprisonment for a jail term not exceeding three years.

sections.label: COVID-19 support schemes rollout
sections.summary: Between February and May 2020, the Government rolled out four Budgets, introducing the Jobs Support Scheme and SkillsFuture Enterprise Credits to help employers pay salaries and training fees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Just between February and May 2020, the Government rolled out four Budgets to provide social support for the vulnerable and increase cashflow to businesses to protect livelihoods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Government introduced the Jobs Support Scheme (JSS) and SkillsFuture Enterprise Credits that helped employers to pay a portion of their workers' salaries and training course fees quickly.

sections.label: IRAS enforcement powers rationale
sections.summary: The passage asks why IRAS needs strong enforcement powers to audit and investigate fraud and abuse cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Why is there a need to grant such strong enforcement powers to IRAS to audit and investigate cases of fraud and abuse?

sections.label: IRAS fraud reports to CAD
sections.summary: From August 2020 to December 2023, IRAS reported 25 suspected abuse or fraud cases to CAD.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: From August 2020 to December 2023, IRAS reported 25 cases of suspected abuse or fraud to CAD.

sections.label: Payout errors and recovery
sections.summary: IRAS paid $31.5 billion for pandemic schemes; AGO found errors under 0.5% of payouts, and 99.7% of wrong payments were recovered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: IRAS paid out $31.5 billion for the Jobs Support Scheme, Rental Cash Grant and Rental Support Scheme during the COVID-19 pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Of these, the Auditor-General's Office (AGO) found errors affecting less than 0.5% of total payouts, as Mr Louis Chua mentioned earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We have since recovered 99.7% of these wrong payments.

sections.label: Grant offences and punishments
sections.summary: Sections 17F(1), 17F(3), 17F(5) set out offences and punishments for obtaining or assisting others to obtain scheduled public scheme grants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Sections 17F(1),17F(3), 17F(5) set out the specific offences and punishments for obtaining or assisting another person to obtain a grant under the scheduled public schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Those convicted may be liable to a penalty equal to one, two or three times the amount of payout overpaid or would have been overpaid, and a monetary fine and/or imprisonment not exceeding three years with the exact terms decided by the Courts.

sections.label: Penalties for convicted grant offenders
sections.summary: Convicted director and accountant face three times payout penalty, fine and/or imprisonment; fund recipient must repay full grant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: For instance, if a director and an accountant of the company were convicted of the most serious grant offence, they will each be liable to a penalty equal to three times of payout overpaid, and a monetary fine and/or imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The party that receives the funds will also be required to repay the full amount of grant that he or she had obtained, in addition to the penalties imposed.
